title: Multi-model assessment of the PDO pattern and its decadal statistics

method.definition: leading EOF of monthly North Pacific SST anomalies, 20N-70N / 110E-100W, global mean anomaly removed, cells weighted by the square root of area
method.common_grid: every source regridded to 1 degree (bilinear) BEFORE the EOF, the observations included; patterns on different grids cannot be correlated and the explained variance is itself grid-dependent
method.amplitude: area-weighted RMS of the pattern regressed on the standardized index, in degC per standard deviation; the index's own standard deviation is 1 by construction and the unit-norm eigenvector carries no physical magnitude
method.sign_convention: positive phase is cool in the central and western North Pacific
method.phase_transitions: sign changes of the 9-year centred running mean, crossings under 3 years apart merged

depends_on_tool_changes: compute_pdo_index now returns a fourth value, the regression pattern in degC per standard deviation. The unit-norm eigenvector it returned before has no physical magnitude, so no amplitude could be reported from the tool as it stood.

The CPC reader gained a 'year_rows' layout, so load_regular_data can return the published PDO file, which is one row per year and one column per month rather than the column layout the Nino products use.
findings: The ERSSTv5 reconstruction correlates with the published series at r = 0.962. That is high, but it is NOT a clean operator validation in the way case T2 is: the published index comes from ERSST v6 and the gridded field here is v5, so the residual mixes a product-version difference with any difference in method. It shows the reconstruction is sound; it cannot separate the two sources of disagreement.
The models place the mode's pattern well: correlations with observations are CESM2 0.925, GFDL-ESM4 0.891, MPI-ESM1-2-LR 0.750, with CESM2 closest.

Reporting the standard deviation of the standardized index would have been vacuous - it is 1 for every source by construction. The amplitude has to come from the regression pattern, which is the only output in physical units: observations show 0.330 degC per standard deviation against CESM2 0.364, GFDL-ESM4 0.291, MPI-ESM1-2-LR 0.409.

The observed phase transitions are [1961, 1976, 2002]. The 1976 one is the documented Pacific climate shift; a 25-year window such as 1990-2014 would not contain it at all, which is why the full record is used.

The models' index series are NOT expected to track the observed one in time, and figure 2 shows that they do not. These are free-running coupled simulations, so their internal variability has its own phasing and is not synchronised with the real world; only a run nudged to observations could be. What is comparable is the PATTERN and the STATISTICS - the variance share, the amplitude, the persistence - which is what steps 2, 3 and 5 measure. A low time correlation between a model index and the observed one is the expected result and not a model failure; the published series is the only line in figure 2 that should track the observed reconstruction, because it is built from nearly the same data.
